summary: Verified the dropdown color bug fix on /admin/team page. Both the Status filter (data-testid='team-status-filter') on the main leads page and the Lead Status select (data-testid='lead-status-select') in LeadDetail view now render with dark blue background (#0a2230) and white text on both the select control and each <option>. Options are readable without needing to hover. Functionality also verified - filter changes and lead status updates work correctly.
critical_code_review_comments: The inline style={{background:'#0a2230', color:'#fff'}} on <option> elements is a pragmatic cross-browser fix (Chrome/Windows respects it, though behavior varies on macOS/Firefox). This is acceptable for the current dark-theme design.
Consider extracting the repeated inline option style into a shared constant or a small <DarkOption> wrapper component for maintainability if more dark-themed selects are added.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Bug fix verified. team-status-filter select: computed bg=rgb(10,34,48), color=rgb(255,255,255); all 7 options have inline background+color set correctly. lead-status-select in LeadDetail: same styling verified across all 6 status options. Filter functionality confirmed (rows update on select). Lead status update confirmed (select_option('contacted') persisted in DOM). Screenshots captured show readable options text on dark background - no white-on-white issue.
rca of the issue: Original issue: default <option> elements inherit browser/OS dropdown styling (typically white background on Windows/Chrome and system-default elsewhere) rather than the parent <select>'s Tailwind bg-white/5 class, because dropdown option lists are rendered by the native OS UI layer. When combined with text-white on the select, options appeared white-on-white. Fix applied by developer: (1) changed select background to solid bg-[#0a2230] (opaque dark blue), and (2) added inline style={background:'#0a2230', color:'#fff'} on each <option> — inline styles on options are the most reliable way to override native dropdown styling in Chromium browsers. Verification confirms options are now readable (white text on dark blue). Mitigation is complete.
